description: "The mission may end, but the story doesn’t have to”. Our team digs into and gives a voice to silent rovers on the Moon and probes drifting past Mars. We are using an interactive website and a Power Point Presentation to educate curious young learners and space enthusiasts so they know these trailblazing machines existed, and what they taught us before going silent.
summary: We are team Astrox8, a group of high-school students, tackling the challenge 'Abandoned but not Forgotten'. We have made a Power Point Presentation and a website according to all the mentioned requirements. Our website (developed with the aid of Artificial Intelligence) helps young learners and space enthusiasts learn more about abandoned space equipment on the Moon and Mars in a simplified format. It is important because most of the data available cannot be clearly understood by them and our website provides a platform where young learners can access easily understand NASA's data in an interactive and concise, visual manner.
details:
Our website 'Sky Sacrifice' is an interactive web page designed specifically for young learners and space enthusiasts to help them learn more about abandoned space equipment, machines, rovers, modules, and spacecraft on the Moon and Mars which are treasured relics and testaments of our exploration far and beyond the Earth, standing still in complete silence for years.

Sky Sacrifice is an immersive web platform that lets users explore these historic sites. It features an archive with telemetry data and vector blueprints, a visual gallery, an educational breakdown of why these missions were abandoned, and a space explorer quiz to engage users with NASA's open data.

The hardware used involves a laptop and a tab. We used HTML and GitHub for coding, Claude and Gemini for refining. We considered that the website needed to be designed specifically for young learners.
